title: The Mill Gap road through the field (the park's Green River Road)
how_read: The park's trace (OpenStreetMap), which Bearss's road matches to 4 m at the median.

title: Bearss's other roads: east to Cherokee Ford, to the Pacolet, to Island Ford, west to Mill Gap
how_read: Separated from the plate by program (solid lines; the contours are dashed), thinned to centre lines, fitted, smoothed; each checked against the 1959 sheet (20-50 m).

title: The same roads beyond Bearss's sheet, as the USGS drew them in 1959
how_read: Picked from the 1959 sheet reprojected to WGS 84; only roads Mills (1825) has leaving the crossroads the same way.

title: Tarleton's approach: today's Green River Road
how_read: Today's road, the playback's reading of the way Tarleton came (CG06).

title: Streams
how_read: Today's streams; they follow the draws of the 1975 photo map and the blue lines of 1959.

title: Rivers, as Mouzon draws them (1775), fitted to today's courses
how_read: Picked by hand every 50-100 pixels of a half-resolution crop and snapped by program to the engraved line; fitted to the ground by matching them to today's rivers (Natural Earth). Rivers with no line in Natural Earth (Pacolet, Tyger, Enoree, Black, Ashley, Combahee) follow the fit and are low.

title: The sea coast, as Mouzon draws it, and the sea
how_read: The outer coast snapped to the engraved line and fitted to today's coast. Inlets, islands and the sounds behind them are not traced yet: the sea is closed across the harbour mouths.

title: The main roads of 1775, as Mouzon draws them
how_read: Picked by hand along Mouzon's double lines every 100-150 pixels (about 9-14 km), not snapped. Good to a few kilometres between the fitted towns and crossings.

title: The Cherokee boundary (to 20 May 1777) and the lines with North Carolina (1735-72)
how_read: Picked by hand; the North Carolina lines fitted to today's state line, which follows them.
